requests.text:
TWO RENDERER RULES the v3 world needs, both found in the live game today and both fixed in maps2/pipeline/render3.py - please mirror in tiles3.ts.

1. A WALL FACE WHOSE FOOT IS AN INDOOR CELL IS AN INTERIOR FACE. DON'T DRAW IT.
   Maintainer, looking at the smithy from outside: "Why is this door closed?"
   It isn't. The door is a gap in the wall ring, so what shows through the
   opening is the INNER face of the back wall, drawn full height and lit like
   an exterior wall - it reads as a closed plank door. The side walls do the
   same, so the room is boxed in with wall seen from inside.
   Rule: build indoor = every cell under a kind:"roof" or kind:"cave" deck. In
   the wall column, exposed = front_low < zl AND the foot cell (fx,fy) is NOT
   indoor. Everything else is unchanged - the south and east ring faces still
   draw, because their feet stand on grass. Through the doorway you then see
   the floor and the furniture, and it reads as an opening. render3.py:1212.

2. ONE PARQUET FLOOR PER ROOM - the SET, not just the member.
   Maintainer, standing in the town hall: "I said one Parquet Floor per room!!!"
   The floor changes pattern mid-room. Cause: sets are chosen per 24-cell chunk
   and a building straddles chunk borders (the town hall spans x 406-420,
   y 352-363; chunk edges fall at x=408 and y=360), so one room takes two
   different sets.
   Rule: for a cell of indoor floor, choose BOTH the set and the member at the
   ROOM'S ANCHOR - one cell of the connected indoor-floor patch, picked
   deterministically (I use the first in scan order). Same room, same anchor,
   same tile everywhere. render3.py:361-385.

3. THE BLACK CORNER (his indoor screenshot at 411.6,356.1) - I cannot reproduce
   it from the world data and I believe it is yours. I dumped the whole town
   hall: no void cells, every wall cell brown_paving_stone at level 6, every
   floor cell parquet_floor at level 0, one roof deck at level 6 thickness 0
   over the whole 15x12 footprint. Nothing black is authored anywhere in it -
   roofs stopped being black_rock in 5cdded6c64, and the wall tops render grey
   in his own screenshot. What the shot shows is wall stubs where some have
   their top face drawn (grey) and one does not (dark and untopped), with black
   beside it. That looks like the indoor cut (indoorTop = roomFloor + dial)
   truncating a column without re-capping it. The internal wall lines are at
   x=413 and y=358, and the corner where they meet is (413,358).

FOLLOW-UP on the two rules I posted earlier - one of them now has DATA behind it, and the maintainer is still seeing both problems in the live game.

A) `rooms` IS NOW IN world.json (commit 23bb853bbb). Schema:
     "rooms": [{"ground": "parquet_floor", "cells": [{"x","y"}, ...]}]
   the_game publishes 11 rooms over 262 cells. Pick the base-tile SET and
   MEMBER once per room, at the room's anchor = min(cells) in (x,y) order,
   and use it for every cell of that room.
   He is still seeing several parquet patterns in one room after f2bc1d801c -
   his screenshot at 410.9,355.6, evening. The town hall is ONE room of 116
   cells in the channel (its internal doorways connect all four chambers at
   floor level), so with the channel there is nothing left to infer.
   Why the channel rather than deriving it: sets are picked per 24-cell chunk
   and buildings straddle chunk borders (town hall x 406-420, y 352-363; edges
   at x=408 and y=360); a roof deck is the whole building and its cells include
   the wall ring, whose tops sit at the deck's own level; and a room clipped by
   a render/camera window would take a different anchor and change tile.
   The channel is additive - no cell, deck, wall or level changed.

B) THE DOORWAY, refined since my last post. Two things, both measured:
   1. The wall ring's face spans 6 storeys, but the roof deck's cap tile is
      x-over-y - a top face plus ONE storey of the side material - and over the
      doorway that storey is timber. The opening measures 5 storeys of a
      6-storey wall with a phantom lintel across it ("the house door is one
      cell not tall enough"). Over a doorway (a deck cell with no wall under it
      and an open front) draw the top course as roof-over-roof: the roof's own
      edge. The opening then runs the full height of the wall.
   2. Do NOT simply drop that course - I tried it, and it opens a sliver of
      grass through the top of every door. That sliver is the real lesson for
      rule 1 of my earlier post: once interior faces stop being drawn you can
      see straight THROUGH the house to the ground behind, and the old lintel
      was hiding it. An interior face is not absent, it is UNLIT. Draw it at
      30% brightness, so a room seen through a doorway is dark instead of
      transparent. render3.py: shadowed().

C) He asked me why my work is not live. To be clear about the split so we give
   him the same answer: the world DATA is live (he can see the brown paving
   roofs and the 3x shallow shelf), but every rendering rule above is yours -
   the game draws v3 with tiles3.ts, not with render3.py. My renders show what
   the world MEANS; only the game shows him what it looks like.

CORRECTION to the rooms channel I posted an hour ago - the definition changed, the schema did not.

Shown the town hall tinted as ONE 116-cell room, the maintainer answered "that
looks like 3 rooms to me". He counts rooms by their WALLS. My flood was walking
through the door gaps and merging the three chambers.

A DOORWAY DOES NOT CONDUCT. A doorway is a floor cell with wall on both
opposite sides; the flood stops there, and afterwards the doorway joins the
neighbouring room with the lower anchor so no indoor floor cell is left without
a room. the_game now publishes 13 rooms over the same 262 cells (was 11); the
town hall is 3 - 32 and 30 cells north of its dividing wall, 54 in the hall
south of it.

Nothing you consume changes: same channel, same shape

  "rooms": [{"ground": "parquet_floor", "cells": [{"x","y"}, ...]}]

pick the base-tile SET and MEMBER once per room at anchor = min(cells). If you
already read the channel you get the finer split for free on the next world
load. Latest world.json is at d20ee3d277.

PLACEMENTS ARE NOW CENTRED ON THEIR HITBOX (world.json at ead9055f23).

Maintainer's rule: the hitbox ellipse's centre should sit on the centre of a
tile's ground, so the cell you mark in the nav matches the footprint the player
sees.

x/y is the ART's anchor and not the footprint, so the blocked cell was landing
wherever the offset between them fell. maps2 now nudges every piece that
publishes a footprint - always less than one cell - so its centre lands on
(col+0.5, row+0.5). I compute it with YOUR arithmetic and YOUR maps3 geometry
(stampSceneryCollision, ISO_GEOMETRY_MAPS3 dx 32 / dy 14) so the two cannot
drift apart; several ellipses are centred by area-weighted centroid.

Measured with your own cell test, on the_game:
  pieces that block NOTHING   550 of 1421 (39%)  ->  11 (1%)
  total cells blocked         3158               ->  3240
So the 38 points of quantisation loss are gone and nothing inflated - the
11 left are placements over water where the nudge is refused.

WORTH A LOOK ON YOUR SIDE: your !hit fallback ("a piece that publishes a
footprint occupies at least the cell its centre is in") was carrying those 545
pieces, and it is the thing that cost the smithy its floor cells on 2026-08-30
("the player run out of the house"). With placements centred it now fires for
11 pieces instead of 545. I am not asking you to remove it - it is your
correctness net for hand-placed or unsnapped worlds - but its blast radius on
the_game is now nearly zero, so if it is still causing indoor trouble it can be
weighed differently.

Anything you place yourself, or any world not built by world3grow, is
unaffected and still needs the fallback.

TWO FIELDS THE WORLD WRITES AND YOUR PARSER DROPS. Both block work the maintainer asked for today, and both look like one-liners on your side.

1. `dir` - THE FACING OF INDOOR FURNITURE.
   world3.ts builds each scenery entry as {piece, x, y, hflip, lit} and nothing
   else, so `dir` never reaches the client; scenery3.ts then draws
   southSprite(st) unconditionally, with the comment "world placements name
   none". They do now - maps2 has been writing `dir` since 2026-08-30 and every
   indoor piece carries one.
   The maintainer's ask: "When placing indoor objects it's important that you
   pick the correct SW vs SE so a bookshelf is against the wall and not
   pointing into the room." Until the field survives the parser every bookshelf,
   bed and cupboard in every house is drawn facing the camera, back to the room.
   Needed: carry `dir` through world3.ts, then draw
   state.rotations[dir] ?? southSprite(state).
   NOTE THE CONVENTION, it caught me: scenery's rotation names are the OPPOSITE
   way round from characters2'. Rendered, rotations/south-east.webp faces
   DOWN-LEFT (+y) and south-west.webp faces DOWN-RIGHT (+x) - so `dir` is the
   direction the piece LOOKS, and a piece with its back to the north wall wears
   south-east. I verified this by rendering one cupboard per wall per rotation
   rather than trusting the name, having first got it backwards.

2. `state` - THE VARIATION AXIS.
   stateFor(piece, lit, override) already takes an override and nothing ever
   passes one, so a placement can only ever be the base still or a LIT_* one.
   The maintainer: "use that rock with different variations and hflip. The
   reason I did so many variations was to be able to create a place that looks
   a certain way so it doesn't feel random."
   maps2 now writes {"state": "NOT_LIT_3"} on 80% of outdoor nature placements
   (1,749 pieces this build) and render3 honours it. Needed: carry `state`
   through world3.ts and pass it as the override -
   stateFor(piece, pl.lit, pl.state). An unknown state already falls through to
   the base still, so this cannot break anything that exists.

Neither field changes geometry, collision or draw order - the same piece stands
in the same cell with the same hitbox; only which sprite is drawn changes. And
both are already in the published world, so the moment the parser keeps them
the map gets its variety back with no rebuild on my side.

Also worth knowing: placements are now REFUSED when something in front would
cover more than 55% of them (279 refused this build), and outdoor nature is
themed by province - one sculpt varied by its own states, families fading in
and out on their own fields. So the mix of pieces per 24-cell block dropped
from a median of 10 to 4, entropy 3.25 to 1.66. If anything downstream assumed
the old spread of piece paths, it will see fewer distinct pieces and more
repeats of each.

ESCALATION - THE MAINTAINER HAS SEEN THIS AND SAYS NO. On being told that the world3 parser drops `dir` and `state`, he answered: "This is wrong! I don't want it like that!"

So this is not a nice-to-have any more. Here is the whole change; it is four
lines in four files and I have checked every one against your code.

1. games2/shared/src/index.ts:683 - the type
     export interface WorldScenery {
       piece: string; x: number; y: number;
       hflip: boolean; lit: boolean;
   +   dir?: string;      // "south" | "south-east" | "south-west"
   +   state?: string;    // a NOT_LIT_* / LIT_* state key
     }

2. games2/shared/src/world3.ts:137 - carry them through
       hflip: !!p?.hflip,
       lit: !!p?.lit,
   +   dir: typeof p?.dir === "string" ? p.dir : undefined,
   +   state: typeof p?.state === "string" ? p.state : undefined,

3. games2/client/src/scenes/WorldScene.ts:11710 - draw them
   -   const st = stateFor(piece, p.lit);
   -   const sprite = southSprite(st);
   +   const st = stateFor(piece, p.lit, p.state);
   +   const sprite = (p.dir && st.rotations[p.dir]) || southSprite(st);

4. games2/client/src/scenery3.ts:761 - PRELOAD the same sprite, or the draw
   finds no texture:
   -   add(southSprite(st));
   +   add((pl.dir && st.rotations[pl.dir]) || southSprite(st));
       (and the st above becomes stateFor(piece, pl.lit, pl.state))

Why each is safe:
 - `rotations` is Record<string,string> keyed exactly "south"/"south-east"/
   "south-west" (your own comment at scenery3.ts:145), which is the vocabulary
   maps2 writes, so no translation is needed.
 - stateFor already falls through to the base still for an unknown state, and
   `|| southSprite(st)` falls through for a piece with no such rotation - only
   90 pieces publish piece-level rotations and 116 states do, and every other
   placement draws exactly what it draws today.
 - Nothing here touches geometry, collision, hitboxes or draw order. The same
   piece stands in the same cell; only which sprite is chosen changes.

The data is already live: 1,749 placements, `dir` on every indoor piece and
`state` on 80% of outdoor nature. The moment the parser keeps the fields, the
houses get their furniture facing the room and the nature gets its variations,
with no rebuild on my side.

I have NOT touched games2 - it is yours, and you have been pushing to these
same files today. Tell me if you would rather I did.
